atoms.a: Coordinative conjunctions are words that link together two clauses.
You can only use coordinative conjunctions in the middle of a sentence.

instruction.text: Fill in the gap with the correct coordinative conjunction.

atoms.a: ssml: She loves her sister, <break time='500ms'/> she loves their dog Marmite more.
atoms.b: She loves her sister, ((++but or)) she loves their dog Marmite more.

atoms.a: ssml: I was very busy,  <break time='500ms'/> I forgot.
atoms.b: I was very busy, ((++so or)) I forgot.

atoms.a: ssml: You should go to bed now, <break time='500ms'/> wake up early tomorrow.
atoms.b: You should go to bed now, ((++and so)) you should wake up early tomorrow.

atoms.a: ssml: I could go to the supermarket, <break time='500ms'/> I could go to the farmers market.
atoms.b: I could go to the supermarket, ((so ++or)) I could go to the farmers market.

atoms.sound: Her new car is red but its not very fast
He does not eat meat, so he is a vegetarian.
Do you prefer Italian food, or do you prefer Japanese food?

atoms.a: She is going to the concert with her sister,
atoms.sound: She is going to the concert with her sister, and she is very excited.
